title: 75% of Users Judge a Company's Credibility by the Design of Its Products. Is Your Design Making a Difference?
description: Users judge a company's credibility by its design: what the Stanford Guidelines say, the role of first impressions and design as a competitive edge.

related.title: WhatsApp Next
related.body: In practice: content, landing page and ads working together, with 1,680 sign-ups in 4 days.

blocks.text: Did you know that 75% of users judge a company's credibility based on the design of its product? This figure, highlighted in a study from the “Stanford Guidelines for Web Credibility”, reinforces how much design shapes users' first perception of a brand. In an increasingly competitive digital world, where first impressions form in seconds, the look of your product can decide whether you win or lose a customer's trust right at first contact.

blocks.text: The Impact of Design on Credibility

According to the study conducted by Stanford University, users tend to trust websites and products with well-crafted, professional design more. That's because attractive and, more importantly, functional design sends a message of seriousness and professionalism. These factors are essential for turning visits into conversions, that is, getting users who arrived at your site or product out of curiosity to become customers.

blocks.text: A practical example can be found in companies like Apple and Airbnb, which are benchmarks when it comes to user-centered design. These brands don't focus only on aesthetics, but on functionality and the smooth experience they provide. And the result? Millions of loyal users who trust and invest in their products.

Have you ever noticed how often we quickly decide whether to trust a brand based only on how it looks? This is explained by our tendency to form first impressions in a matter of seconds. According to a study published in the Behaviour & Information Technology journal, users take less than 50 milliseconds to form an opinion about a website. And that opinion is often directly tied to design.

blocks.caption: The first impression becomes brand perception.

blocks.text: If your product or site looks confusing, with hard navigation and cluttered visuals, users may associate that with a lack of organization in your company as a whole, and lose trust right away. On the other hand, a clear, functional design sends the message that your company is trustworthy, professional and efficient.

Beyond credibility, design can be a competitive edge. Companies that invest in design see, on average, a 32% increase in revenue. That's because design not only improves the user experience, it also makes it easier to communicate the product's value and raises perceived quality. A McKinsey & Company study found that design-driven companies, meaning those that put design at the center of their strategy, perform up to twice as well as those that don't.
So design goes far beyond looks. It's a strategic tool to add value to the product, stand out from the competition and, of course, build customer trust.
How Much Do You Invest in Your Company's Design?

The question that remains is: how much are you investing in your product's design? If you're not yet treating design as a fundamental piece of your strategy, you may be missing valuable opportunities to build a stronger, longer-lasting connection with your customers.

Investing in design doesn't just mean having something pretty, but making sure the user experience is flawless and that your brand's credibility grows stronger from the first contact. And, as the numbers show, that can be the difference between a company that just “exists” and a company that truly wins people over.
